slides.say: A B C is a right triangle whose sides A B and A C are tangent to a circle with center O, at B and at D. B, O, E and C lie on one straight line, and E is on the circle. Given, O E and E C are both four centimeters. What is the area of the shaded region between C D, C E and the minor arc D E, in square centimeters?
at: A B C is a right triangle

slides.say: The minor arc is the small arc between D and E. So it's a shaded-area question again, and we need a scheme, what minus what.
at: The minor arc is the small arc

slides.say: [short pause] The problem is that here the scheme isn't clear. Is it the big triangle minus a few pieces? It's not clear yet.
What do we do in cases like this? We work with the givens, we put them on the figure, and we hope the solution shows itself.
A B is tangent to the circle at B. B is a point of tangency, and the right angle is already marked there, because the radius O B is perpendicular to the tangent.
at: the right angle is already marked

slides.say: D is also a point of tangency, but there's no radius to it. So we add the automatic construction, from O to D.
That's the radius O D, and we mark the right angle at D. It's the most basic construction there is.
How long is the radius? O E is a radius, and it's four. So O D is a radius too, and it's four.
at: So O D is a radius too

slides.say: And now the scheme is clear. Take triangle O D C, and remove the sector D O E. What's left is exactly the shaded part. It's just like the last question.
[pause] Let's look at triangle O D C on its own, bigger. It has a right angle at D. One leg, O D, is four. The hypotenuse O C is O E plus E C, four plus four, eight.
at: Let's look at triangle O D C

slides.say: The area of a right triangle is leg times leg, over two. So we need the other leg, D C. Pythagoras would work, but there's no need.

Look, the hypotenuse is exactly twice the leg, eight and four. That happens only in a gold triangle, the thirty, sixty, ninety triangle. So the angle opposite the short leg, at C, is thirty degrees. And the angle opposite D C, at O, is sixty degrees.
at: So the angle opposite the short leg

slides.say: In a gold triangle, the long leg is root three times the short leg. So D C is four root three.
at: So D C is four root three

slides.say: Leg times leg, over two. Four times four root three is sixteen root three, and over two it's eight root three.
Should we find the sector now? We saw in the last question that we can stop halfway and look at the choices. We're looking for eight root three, minus something with pi.
at: We're looking for eight root three

slides.say: Choice number two has sixteen root three, and choice number four has four root three. Neither has eight root three, so they're both out.
But this time the trick doesn't finish the job. Two choices start with eight root three, choice number one and choice number three. So we need the sector too.
The sector is a part of the circle. The whole circle is pi r squared, pi times four squared, sixteen pi.

Which part? The central angle D O E is sixty degrees, and sixty out of three hundred sixty is a sixth. A sixth of sixteen pi is sixteen pi over six. Divide the top and the bottom by two, and it's eight pi over three.

Choice number one has four pi over three. That's only half of our sector, so it's out. Only choice number three has both parts right, eight root three minus eight pi over three. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: By the way, some students find the sector first. Then they look for something minus eight pi over three, and that rules out choice number one and choice number four. Here we need both parts, and together they leave only choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: some students find the sector first
